title: the Green Zone Rising
premise: Jude Zhou, a traumatized interpreter embedded with a doomed peace delegation in a contested border city, discovers that a voiceprint harvested from his own intercepted transmissions has unlocked a server belonging to Meridian, the covert network that trained him as a child asset and now trades in engineered conflicts. Hunted by his former handlers and distrusted by the delegation he's supposed to protect, Jude must decide whether to stay invisible or weaponize the one thing they never revoked: his access. As the checkpoint schedule shifts and the delegation's collapse accelerates, he burns Meridian's archive from inside their own safehouse, trading his anonymity for the survival of everyone at the crossing. The novel ends with Jude walking through the checkpoint as a named man, carrying nothing but a printed list of the children Meridian still holds.
about_author: Orsen Montrose is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent six years attached to humanitarian missions across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose languages are both their livelihood and their cage.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Silence
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Introduces Jude sleepless in a border-city hotel, interpreting preliminary talks he knows are theater. He flinches at a voice on a recording, hinting at 'the incident.' Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Delegation of the Doomed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The peace delegation arrives amid curfew rumors; lead negotiator Amara Osei senses the other side is stalling. Jude translates a veiled threat and realizes someone scripted it. Beat: unease sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine encrypted briefing pings his earpiece with an authentication request: his own voice, sampled years ago, unlocks a server pinged from another continent. Beat: vertigo—the past has a key to his present.

chapters.title: The Incident, Partially Remembered
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: fragmented flashbacks of a training compound, a boy reciting phrases in four languages, a night that went wrong. Present-day Jude vomits after the session. Beat: trauma surfacing against his will.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following the server trace, he finds the name Meridian in an old contact protocol buried in his translation software. He understands he was never just recruited—he was inventory. Beat: cold recognition.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Alpha
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. She watches Jude handle a hostile liaison with impossible fluency and starts a quiet file on him. The checkpoint's shift schedule is announced—six days until rotation. Beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Someone Is Listening
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. His hotel room is searched; nothing taken, everything photographed. A note in his childhood training cipher appears under the door: STAY INVISIBLE. Beat: hunted without proof.

chapters.title: The Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A phone call from Voss, his former handler, offering protection in exchange for silence about the server. Jude records it. Beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara confronts Jude with her file; instead of exposing him, she proposes an alliance—she needs to know who's sabotaging the talks, he needs cover. Beat: wary trust kindled.

chapters.title: What the Server Holds
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Through a proxy terminal he glimpses the archive: biometric files, sleeper protocols, dozens of children currently 'in training.' One name matches a young delegate's aide. Beat: stakes become human.

chapters.title: The Aide
chapters.summary: Aide Lena Kovač's POV. Lena, nineteen, fluent beyond her years, notices Jude watching her. She tests him with a phrase only Meridian children would know. Beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Voss learns Jude accessed the archive; a kill order is drafted under the guise of a security incident at the talks. Jude's diplomatic immunity quietly evaporates. Beat: the net closes.

chapters.title: Night Market
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena leads Jude through smuggler stalls to a data broker who can copy the archive—if they can reach the Meridian safehouse before the checkpoint shift changes. Beat: fragile hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Talks Collapse
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Engineered leaks detonate the negotiation; Amara realizes the collapse was choreographed by someone feeding both sides. She suspects Meridian; she can't prove it. Beat: despair hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Safehouse Reconnaissance
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude maps the safehouse—a converted clinic three streets from Checkpoint Alpha—and identifies its one blind window and its guard rotation. Beat: methodical courage replacing panic.

chapters.title: Voss at the Door
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss visits Jude personally, nostalgic and menacing, reminding him what Meridian made him and what it can unmake. Jude plays compliant while copying Voss's access badge frequency. Beat: the mask held by a thread.

chapters.title: Lena's Price
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena confesses she was activated last year—that some of the sabotage ran through her. She offers her handler's credentials to Jude. Beat: guilt transmuted into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Curfew
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Citywide curfew traps the trio in a basement as patrols sweep for 'unregistered interpreters.' They pass the hours telling each other the truth. Beat: intimacy forged in fear.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara decodes enough of Meridian's pattern to predict which delegates will be disappeared next; her own name is on the list. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: Halfway Point: The Copy Begins
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Using Voss's badge clone, Jude enters the safehouse at 3 a.m. and begins exfiltrating the archive to a burner drive. Progress bar: forty percent. Beat: breathless control.

chapters.title: Alarm
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A motion sensor trips; Jude hides in a supply closet as guards sweep, listening to them discuss his own death warrant. Beat: terror in stillness.

chapters.title: Extraction Interrupted
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena triggers a diversionary fire alarm across the district to pull guards out; she's detained at a perimeter check. Beat: heroism with a cost.

chapters.title: Seventy Percent
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Back inside, Jude resumes the copy but finds the archive partitioned—one segment requires a live voiceprint spoken in the room. His own. Beat: the trap reveals its design.

chapters.title: Speaking the Key
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude speaks the authentication phrase aloud, knowing it logs his presence permanently. The final segment downloads. Somewhere, Voss is alerted. Beat: irrevocable commitment.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Interrogated in a Meridian front office, Lena stalls by mis-translating deliberately, buying hours. Her handler hesitates—she is, technically, still an asset. Beat: cunning as resistance.

chapters.title: Amara Goes Public
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara briefs a trusted journalist with partial evidence, gambling that sunlight will slow Meridian's cleanup operation. Beat: hope as strategy.

chapters.title: The Delegation Evacuates
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The delegation is ordered out via Checkpoint Alpha before the shift change; Jude must choose between boarding the convoy and finishing the burn. Beat: the fork in the road.

chapters.title: Voss's Gambit
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss offers Jude full reinstatement, a new identity, and Lena's release—for the drive. Jude says yes. Beat: the reader doubts him; so does Voss.

chapters.title: The Handover That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the exchange, Jude hands over a corrupted decoy drive seeded with a tracer. Voss pockets it smiling. Beat: deception as love letter to the dead self.

chapters.title: Lena Freed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Released as promised, Lena finds Jude and delivers the location of the live training site—children still inside, including her younger brother. Beat: grief with coordinates.

chapters.title: Countdown to Shift Change
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interleave. Fourteen hours until the checkpoint shifts; the burn must happen before Meridian migrates servers. Everyone converges on the safehouse. Beat: acceleration.

chapters.title: The Burn
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Inside the safehouse, Jude executes the wipe—archives, protocols, sleeper activations—watching twenty years of Meridian dissolve into static. Alarms scream. Beat: catharsis through destruction.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Confrontation chapter, Jude vs. Voss, knives-out verbal duel in three languages. Voss realizes the tracer drive led Meridian's response team straight into the burning building. Beat: the student surpassing the maker.

chapters.title: Fire and Extraction
chapters.summary: Jude and Lena escape the collapsing safehouse through the blind window as Meridian's own cleanup crew arrives to find ash. Beat: survival bought with scars.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Alpha, Morning
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. At the checkpoint, Amara uses her remaining authority to get Jude and Lena processed as protected persons, defying orders. Beat: institutional courage.

chapters.title: The Children's Site
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Coordinates passed to an international task force; a raid liberates the training compound. Lena's brother walks out blinking into daylight. Beat: grief answered, not erased.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Testifying under his real name for the first time since childhood, Jude reads the incident aloud in all four languages. Beat: reclamation of voice.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena and Jude reckon with what they did to survive—people used, truths bent—and whether belonging is something you're given or built. Beat: mourning and tenderness.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude walks through Checkpoint Alpha as the shifts change, carrying only a printed list of names still unaccounted for. He sleeps, finally, on the far side. Beat: quiet triumph.

chapters.title: Green Zone Rising
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Amara's POV. Months later, the green zone grows a few blocks wider; Amara receives a postcard from Jude—no return address, just a child's drawing of a checkpoint with the barrier drawn open. Beat: earned, guarded hope.
